vulnerability.title: Add noexec Option to /home
vulnerability.description: The noexec mount option can be used to prevent binaries from being executed out of /home. Add the noexec option to the fourth column of /etc/fstab for the line which controls mounting of /home.
vulnerability.recommendation: Remediation script: # Remediation is applicable only in certain platforms if ( ! In case it is not defined, the # remediation aborts and no changes regarding the mount point are done. mount_point_match_regexp="$(printf "^[[:space:]]*[^#].*[[:space:]]%s[[:space:]]" "/home")" grep "$mount_point_match_regexp" -q /etc/fstab \ || { echo "The mount point '/home' is not even in /etc/fstab, so we can't set up mount options" >&2; echo "Not

triage_decision.reason: The noexec mount option prevents binaries in /home from being executed, reducing risk of privilege escalation and arbitrary code execution from malicious binaries placed in home directories.

reasoning_messages.reasoning:
We need to output a JSON object with plan_description and commands list.
We need to propose a fix for finding: mount_option_home_noexec (rule ID: xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_rule_mount_option_home_noexec). The finding: The noexec mount option missing in /home. The fix: add noexec option to the fourth column of /etc/fstab for the line which controls mounting of /home.

Thus we need to edit /etc/fstab, add noexec to mount options for the line mounting /home.

Assume /etc/fstab line currently something like: UUID=... /home ext4 defaults 0 0 (or maybe just: /home ext4 defaults 0 0). We need to add noexec to the mount options (the fourth field). So we need to change line: from something like UUID=... /home ext4 defaults 0 0 to UUID=... /home ext4 defaults,noexec 0 0.

We don't have actual UUID, but we can use a generic pattern: we can use sed to replace line matching /home.

Better: use sed -i to modify line: s|^\([^ ]\+[[:space:]]\+[^ ]\+[[:space:]]\+/home[[:space:]]| ... But easier: we can use sed -i to add noexec to the mount options field for the line containing /home.

Simplify: Assume line: UUID=... /home ext4 defaults 0 0. We'll change to UUID=... /home ext4 defaults,noexec 0 0.

Thus command: sed -i -E 's|^(\([^ ]\+[[:space:]]\+[^ ]\+[[:space:]]\+/home[[:space:]]).*|\1,noexec|' /etc/fstab

But we need to preserve rest of line.

Alternatively: use awk: awk -i '$2=="/home"{$4=$4",noexec"}1' /etc/fstab

Simpler: Use sed to insert noexec after the third field: sed -i -E 's|^([^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+/home[[:space:]]).*|\1,noexec|' /etc/fstab.

We'll provide a plan with description and commands.

Let's propose:

plan_description: "Add noexec mount option to the /home entry in /etc/fstab to mitigate risk of privilege escalation from executables in home directories."

commands: array of command objects.

We'll have one command: run_cmd with command string: "sed -i -E 's|^([^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+/home[[:space:]]).*|\1,noexec|' /etc/fstab"

We need to ensure proper JSON escaping.

Thus final JSON:

{
  "plan_description": "Add noexec mount option to the /home entry in /etc/fstab to mitigate risk of privilege escalation from executables in home directories.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "command": "sed -i -E 's|^([^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+/home[[:space:]]).*|\1,noexec|' /etc/fstab"
    }
  ]
}

Make sure no extra quotes inside.
